attractions.name: Window Rock Trail
attractions.description: Pinyon-juniper woodland leads to views of Monument and Wedding Canyons and Independence Monument.

attractions.name: Canyon Rim Trail
attractions.description: The cliff-edge route above Wedding Canyon connects Saddlehorn Visitor Center and Book Cliffs View.

attractions.name: Alcove Nature Trail
attractions.description: A box-canyon alcove introduces the monument's plants, animals and rocks. The source describes assistance up to the overlook.
attractions.accessibility: NPS describes access with assistance up to the overlook; this does not establish independent wheelchair suitability.

attractions.name: Otto's Trail
attractions.description: Woodlands open to views of Sentinel Spire, Pipe Organ, Praying Hands and Independence Monument.

attractions.name: Coke Ovens Trail
attractions.description: A descending hillside route reaches an overlook of rounded Wingate Sandstone formations shaped by weathering.

attractions.name: CCC Trail
attractions.description: This ascending connection links Black Ridge Trail with Monument Canyon Trail.

attractions.name: Devils Kitchen Trail
attractions.description: Carved slickrock steps lead toward the natural opening enclosed by tall upright boulders.

attractions.name: Serpents Trail
attractions.description: Sixteen switchbacks follow a historic early-twentieth-century road through Wingate Sandstone.

attractions.name: Echo Canyon Trail
attractions.description: The route leaves Old Gordon Trail for a shady canyon and a seasonal pool beneath cottonwoods; poison ivy is noted near the canyon head.

conflicts.detail: Numeric length withheld: conflicting miles and kilometres. See the official guide; no correction or conversion was imposed.

attractions.name: Crater Rim Trail
attractions.description: A paved circuit on the volcanic rim has steep climbs and descents and interprets the Raton-Clayton Volcanic Field.

attractions.name: Crater Vent Trail
attractions.description: The paved descent reaches the bottom of Capulin's crater; the source reports a 100-foot elevation change.

attractions.name: Lava Flow Trail
attractions.description: An unimproved circuit at the base crosses a lava flow and offers views of volcanic topography.

attractions.name: Boca Trail
attractions.description: This unimproved circuit explores the vent area from which Capulin's lava flows originated.

attractions.name: Nature Trail
attractions.description: A figure-eight sidewalk beside the visitor center interprets plants, wildlife and geology around a volcanic squeeze-up.
attractions.accessibility: NPS describes this figure-eight sidewalk as accessible. Paving alone is not used as proof of accessibility.

attractions.name: Wijiji Trail
attractions.description: The shortest of Chaco's four backcountry hikes explores the wider Chacoan landscape beyond the loop road.
attractions.permitNotes: The source requires each backcountry hiking group to sign in at its trailhead. Check current official requirements.

attractions.name: South Mesa Trail
attractions.description: This backcountry loop begins at the Casa Rinconada parking area and explores the mesa landscape.
attractions.permitNotes: The source requires each backcountry hiking group to sign in at its trailhead. Check current official requirements.

attractions.name: Pueblo Alto Trail
attractions.description: A mesa-top loop offers an elevated view of Pueblo Bonito and context for Chacoan great houses and roads.
attractions.permitNotes: The source requires each backcountry hiking group to sign in at its trailhead. Check current official requirements.

attractions.name: Peñasco Blanco Trail
attractions.description: The longest of the four backcountry hikes presents the scale of Chaco's great-house and road landscape.
attractions.permitNotes: The source requires each backcountry hiking group to sign in at its trailhead. Check current official requirements.

attractions.name: Coleman House Trail
attractions.description: The wooded route reaches the Coleman House site, where enslaved Hannah Reynolds received the wound that killed her during the battle.

attractions.name: Conner-Sweeney Cabin Trail
attractions.description: Fields and woodland provide views of the Conner-Sweeney Cabin, with a possible connection to the Sweeney Trail.

attractions.name: Ferguson Wildlife Trail
attractions.description: Interpretive stops describe habitats around Ferguson field, managed for native pollinators and grassland birds.

attractions.name: Grant’s Approach Trail
attractions.description: Historic Sears Lane and monuments interpret the route Grant traveled toward his meeting with Lee.

attractions.name: Lee’s Headquarters Trail
attractions.description: A short wooded route reaches the marker for Lee's headquarters; roots and rocks remain on the tread.

attractions.name: Southside Connector Trail
attractions.description: Rolling wooded terrain connects Grant's Approach and Tobacco Prizery trails; rocky tread and flood-prone sections require care.

attractions.name: Stage Road Trail
attractions.description: The historic Lynchburg-Richmond Stage Road crosses the village toward the Appomattox River.

attractions.name: Sweeney Trail
attractions.description: Open fields connect the Artillery Park, Charles Sweeney Cabin, Sweeney Cemetery and Conner House site.

attractions.name: Tibbs Trail
attractions.description: Field and forest link the Confederate Cemetery and Appomattox Wayside; the route can combine with Stage Road.

attractions.name: Tobacco Prizery Nature Trail
attractions.description: Interpretation identifies trees and changes in land use; uneven ground and two stair sets have no handrails.

attractions.name: USCT Approach Trail
attractions.description: Open fields trace the approach of United States Colored Troops who helped block the Confederate escape route on April 9, 1865.

attractions.name: Antietam Remembered
attractions.description: A paved walkway links landmarks near the visitor center, including Dunker Church and the Maryland State Monument.

attractions.name: Bloody Lane Trail
attractions.description: The route crosses the historic Mumma and Roulette Farms toward the Confederate position at the Sunken Road.

attractions.name: Cornfield Trail
attractions.description: Starting at Auto Tour Stop 4, the loop interprets the battlefield's early morning fighting.

attractions.name: Final Attack Trail
attractions.description: From Auto Tour Stop 8, this walk follows fields of the final Union advance and Confederate counterattack.

attractions.name: Sherrick Farm Trail
attractions.description: Farm fields and woodlots lead toward Burnside Bridge; use care crossing modern Burnside Bridge Road.

attractions.name: Snavely Ford Trail
attractions.description: Much of this shady loop follows Antietam Creek, with an uphill climb near the end.

attractions.name: Three Farms Trail
attractions.description: This connection links the northern Bloody Lane Trail to the southern Sherrick Farm Trail.

attractions.name: Tidball Trail
attractions.description: The route begins at Newcomer House and reaches a battlefield overlook near the Union Fifth Corps crossing.

attractions.name: Union Advance Trail
attractions.description: The walk crosses Burnside Bridge to examine Confederate defenses and Union Ninth Corps approaches.

attractions.name: West Woods Trail
attractions.description: A mostly shaded circuit from Auto Tour Stop 5 explores key locations of fighting in the West Woods.

attractions.name: Heppe Cave Trail
attractions.description: Ponderosa pines, mountain mahogany and juniper lead toward a large lava-tube collapse and Heppe Ice Cave.

attractions.name: Gillem Bluff Trail
attractions.description: The climb reaches the top of Gillem Bluff with expansive landscape views.

attractions.name: Schonchin Butte Trail
attractions.description: A climb up a cinder cone reaches a historic fire lookout structure and views over the basin.

attractions.name: Missing Link Trail
attractions.description: This connection joins the Three Sisters and Bunchgrass routes and can form part of a longer loop.

attractions.name: Symbol Bridge Trail
attractions.description: Lava-tube collapses and pictographs are visible near Symbol Bridge Cave and Big Painted Cave.

attractions.name: Bunchgrass Trail
attractions.description: Open brushlands and juniper thickets connect the campground to Bunchgrass overlook.

attractions.name: Thomas-Wright Battlefield Trail
attractions.description: Interpretation connects Modoc War history with examples of volcanism; wildflowers are described for late spring and early summer.

attractions.name: Black Crater Trail
attractions.description: A spur from Thomas-Wright Battlefield Trail reaches a spatter cone and lava tree molds.

conflicts.detail: Numeric length withheld: typographic conflict in published mileage. See the official guide; no correction or conversion was imposed.

attractions.name: Big Nasty Trail
attractions.description: Rough lava, crater-rim views and ponderosa forests characterize a loop near Mammoth Crater and Hidden Valley.

attractions.name: Whitney Butte Trail
attractions.description: The route curves around Whitney Butte toward the western wilderness boundary, with views of Mount Shasta and Callahan Lava Flow.

attractions.name: Three Sisters Trail
attractions.description: Collapsed lava-tube trenches thread through juniper and sagebrush wilderness; connecting routes form a longer loop.

attractions.name: Lyons Trail
attractions.description: A former monument road crosses much of the park from north to south through wilderness.

attractions.name: Prairie Vista
attractions.description: Waysides interpret prairie grasslands on a loop starting near the visitor center.

attractions.name: Elk Mountain
attractions.description: A campground loop follows the meeting of grassland and forest; elk bugling may be heard in autumn.

attractions.name: Rankin Ridge
attractions.description: A nature loop reaches the park's highest point and distant views; the fire tower itself is closed.

attractions.name: Wind Cave Canyon
attractions.description: A former road follows limestone cliffs and forested hillsides toward the park boundary.

attractions.name: Cold Brook Canyon
attractions.description: Ponderosa forest gives way to prairie and a prairie-dog town along the canyon.

conflicts.detail: Numeric length withheld: inconsistent miles and kilometres. See the official guide; no correction or conversion was imposed.

attractions.name: Lookout Point
attractions.description: Rolling prairie descends toward Beaver Creek and connects to longer loop options.

attractions.name: East Bison Flats
attractions.description: A steep climb from Wind Cave Canyon leads into rolling prairie and views of Buffalo Gap and the Black Hills.

attractions.name: Sanctuary
attractions.description: Rolling prairie and a large prairie-dog town lead toward the Highland Creek junction.

attractions.name: Centennial
attractions.description: This park segment forms part of the much longer Black Hills Centennial Trail, crossing prairie, pine forest and Beaver Creek.

attractions.name: Highland Creek
attractions.description: The park's longest trail crosses mixed-grass prairie, ponderosa forest and riparian habitats.

attractions.name: Boland Ridge
attractions.description: A succession of climbs affords Black Hills, Red Valley and prairie panoramas.

attractions.name: Beaver Pond Nature Trail
attractions.description: Yucca flats and a ridge above Lime Kiln Creek lead down a steep hillside to beaver ponds and evidence of dam-building.

attractions.name: Bighorn Head Gate
attractions.description: A gravel path reaches remnants of an early-twentieth-century irrigation system. Water levels can submerge the head gate.

attractions.name: Three Mile Access
attractions.description: A riverside path follows the Bighorn River to a cottonwood grove, with opportunities to observe fishing and waterbirds.

attractions.name: Visitor Center Pond
attractions.description: A concrete loop behind the Lovell visitor center circles a former solar-reflection pond now returning toward marsh habitat.
attractions.accessibility: The official guide labels this route accessible; detailed slope, surface and assistance requirements are not provided.

attractions.name: Sykes Mountain Trail
attractions.description: A rugged desert-mountain ascent reaches overlooks of Bighorn Canyon and Horseshoe Bend; summer heat is a particular concern.

attractions.name: Mouth of the Canyon Trail
attractions.description: Views of the Pryor and Bighorn Mountains contrast with red Chugwater outcrops near Horseshoe Bend.

attractions.name: State Line Trail
attractions.description: Juniper scrubland and limestone plateaus lead to a canyon-rim view, with a connection toward Ranger Delight.

attractions.name: Ranger Delight
attractions.description: A faint road cut and saddle lead toward the canyon rim from near the Montana state line.

evidence.name: Ranger Delight
evidence.measurementBasis: published as round; return basis not further specified

attractions.name: Sullivan's Knob Trail
attractions.description: A canyon-rim walk passes near the ancient Bad Pass Trail, seasonally used by Indigenous travelers between the Bighorn Basin and Northern Plains.

attractions.name: Two Eagles Interpretive Trail
attractions.description: Interpretation explains stone circles left by Indigenous families who weighted tipi edges with stones. These cultural resources must remain in place.
attractions.accessibility: The official guide labels this route accessible; detailed slope, surface and assistance requirements are not provided.

attractions.name: Lower Layout Creek Trail
attractions.description: An old two-track road follows the area south of Layout Creek, with views into Layout Creek Canyon.

attractions.name: Upper Layout Creek Trail
attractions.description: A steep hike explores Layout Creek’s water and ranching landscape, whose irrigation history includes Erastus Ewing’s 1897 water claim.

attractions.name: Barry's Island Trail
attractions.description: A former two-track road circles Chain Canyon, once used by cattle rustlers, toward Barry’s Island; high reservoir water may cover parts of the route.

attractions.name: Paved Path to Canyon Overlook
attractions.description: The path from the visitor center reaches views of Square Tower Group structures and native-plant interpretation.
attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Square Tower Loop Trail
attractions.description: Primitive slickrock and packed dirt circle ancestral Puebloan structures, with a steep canyon crossing.
attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Hovenweep Castle Hike (Out-and-Back)
attractions.description: A shorter route from Canyon Overlook uses the Square Tower Loop to view Hovenweep Castle and nearby structures.
attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Horseshoe and Hackberry Trail (Out-and-Back)
attractions.description: Packed dirt, sandy wash and slickrock connect Horseshoe House and the larger Hackberry sacred site.
attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Hiking at Holly (Out-and-Back hike from Holly parking area)
attractions.description: The primitive route passes Holly Tower and Holly House and ends at a petroglyph panel beneath an overhang.

evidence.name: Hiking at Holly (Out-and-Back hike from Holly parking area)

attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Hiking to Holly (Out-and-Back hike from campground)
attractions.description: The Keely Canyon route passes narrow boulder slots and partly crosses Bureau of Land Management land on its way to Holly.

evidence.name: Hiking to Holly (Out-and-Back hike from campground)

attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.

attractions.name: Hiking at Cajon (Out-and-Back)
attractions.description: A mostly flat slickrock path winds around ancestral structures with broad canyon-country views.
attractions.seasonalNotes: Trails are described as daylight-only; remain on designated paths and do not enter structures.
